#the two files are total immigration and total emigration over 2015-2024
# data sources: VAN1AAR and VAN2AAR. 

immigration = pd.read_csv('immigration2024.csv', header=None, encoding='ISO-8859-1')
immigration.columns = ['Citizenship', 'Immigration']
emigration = pd.read_csv('emigration2024.csv', header=None, encoding='ISO-8859-1')
emigration.columns = ['Citizenship', 'Emigration']
# Merge the two DataFrames on the 'citizenship' column
merged_df = pd.merge(immigration, emigration, on='Citizenship')

merged_df['Net migration'] = merged_df['Immigration'] - merged_df['Emigration']

# Sort by 'Net migration' in descending order
merged_df = merged_df.sort_values(by='Net migration', ascending=False)

# Drop rows with a 0 or NaN 'Immigration'
merged_df = merged_df[merged_df['Immigration'].notna() & (merged_df['Immigration'] != 0)]

# Reset index
merged_df = merged_df.reset_index(drop=True)

# URL to the GeoJSON file for country boundaries
geojson_url = 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python-visualization/folium/master/examples/data/world-countries.json'

# Fetch GeoJSON data
response = requests.get(geojson_url)
geojson_data = response.json()

# Mapping of country names to align with GeoJSON names
country_name_mapping = {
    'USA': 'United States of America',
    # Add other mappings if necessary
}

# Replace names in the dataframe to align with GeoJSON
merged_df['Citizenship'] = merged_df['Citizenship'].replace(country_name_mapping)

# Initialize a folium map
m = folium.Map(location=[20, 0], zoom_start=2)

# FIRST: Add the Net_migration property to GeoJSON features
for feature in geojson_data['features']:
    country_name = feature['properties']['name']
    # Find the matching 'Net migration' value for each country
    migration_value = merged_df.loc[merged_df['Citizenship'] == country_name, 'Net migration']
    # If there's a match, add it as a string to the GeoJSON feature; otherwise, set as 'N/A'
    feature['properties']['Net_migration'] = (
        str(migration_value.values[0]) if not migration_value.empty else 'N/A'
    )

# Create a custom style function for countries
def style_function(feature):
    country_name = feature['properties']['name']
    migration_value = merged_df.loc[merged_df['Citizenship'] == country_name, 'Net migration']
    
    if migration_value.empty:
        return {'fillColor': '#F5F5F5', 'color': 'gray', 'weight': 0.5, 'fillOpacity': 0.7}
    
    value = migration_value.values[0]
    
    # Assign dark purple to negative values
    if value < 0:
        return {'fillColor': '#4B0082', 'color': 'black', 'weight': 0.5, 'fillOpacity': 0.7}
    
    # For positive values, use a logarithmic scale
    if value > 0:
        # Take log10, with a small offset to avoid log(0)
        log_value = np.log10(value + 1)  # +1 to handle small positive values
        max_log = np.log10(merged_df[merged_df['Net migration'] > 0]['Net migration'].max() + 1)
        
        # Normalize to 0-1 range
        normalized = log_value / max_log
        
        # Create a yellow-to-green gradient based on log value
        # Yellow for small values, dark green for large values
        r = int(255 * (1 - normalized * 0.7))  # Reduce red as value increases
        g = int(255 * (0.7 + normalized * 0.3))  # Keep green high
        b = int(normalized * 60)  # Add a bit of blue for darker greens
        
        color = f'#{r:02x}{g:02x}{b:02x}'
        return {'fillColor': color, 'color': 'black', 'weight': 0.5, 'fillOpacity': 0.7}
    
    # For zero values
    return {'fillColor': '#FFFFBF', 'color': 'black', 'weight': 0.5, 'fillOpacity': 0.7}

# Add the custom-styled GeoJSON layer
folium.GeoJson(
    geojson_data,
    style_function=style_function,
    tooltip=folium.GeoJsonTooltip(
        fields=['name'],
        aliases=['Country:']
    )
).add_to(m)

# THEN: Add tooltips with Net_migration field AFTER it's been added to the GeoJSON
folium.GeoJson(
    geojson_data,
    style_function=lambda x: {'fillColor': 'transparent', 'color': 'transparent', 'weight': 0},
    tooltip=folium.GeoJsonTooltip(
        fields=['name', 'Net_migration'],
        aliases=['Country:', 'Net Migration:']
    )
).add_to(m)

# Create a custom legend
legend_html = '''
<div style="position: fixed; 
     bottom: 50px; left: 50px; width: 180px; height: 160px; 
     border:2px solid grey; z-index:9999; font-size:14px;
     background-color: white;
     padding: 10px;
     border-radius: 5px;">
     
     <span style="font-weight: bold;">Net Migration</span><br>
     <i style="background: #4B0082; width: 15px; height: 15px; display: inline-block;"></i> Negative<br>
     <i style="background: #FFFFBF; width: 15px; height: 15px; display: inline-block;"></i> Near Zero<br>
     <i style="background: #D9EF8B; width: 15px; height: 15px; display: inline-block;"></i> Low<br>
     <i style="background: #A6D96A; width: 15px; height: 15px; display: inline-block;"></i> Medium<br>
     <i style="background: #66BD63; width: 15px; height: 15px; display: inline-block;"></i> High<br>
     <i style="background: #1A9850; width: 15px; height: 15px; display: inline-block;"></i> Very High<br>
     
</div>
'''

m.get_root().html.add_child(folium.Element(legend_html))

# Save the map to an HTML file
m.save('net_migration_map_2024.html')

# Display the map
m

# Initialize a folium map
m = folium.Map(location=[20, 0], zoom_start=2)

# Add a new property to each feature in the geojson for 'Percentage stay' value
for feature in geojson_data['features']:
    country_name = feature['properties']['name']
    # Find the matching 'Percentage stay' value for each country
    stay_value = merged_df.loc[merged_df['Citizenship'] == country_name, 'Percentage stay']
    # If there's a match, add it as a string to the GeoJSON feature; otherwise, set as 'N/A'
    feature['properties']['Percentage stay'] = (
        str(stay_value.values[0]) if not stay_value.empty else 'N/A'
    )

# Find the minimum and maximum values
min_val = merged_df['Percentage stay'].min()
max_val = merged_df['Percentage stay'].max()

# Create a choropleth map with a built-in colormap
choropleth = folium.Choropleth(
    geo_data=geojson_data,
    name='choropleth',
    data=merged_df,
    columns=['Citizenship', 'Percentage stay'],
    key_on='feature.properties.name',
    fill_color='RdYlBu_r' if min_val < 0 else 'YlOrRd',  # Use diverging colormap if negative values exist
    fill_opacity=0.7,
    line_opacity=0.2,
    legend_name='Percentage Stay (%)',
    highlight=True,
    nan_fill_color='#F5F5F5'  # Light gray for NaN values
).add_to(m)

# If we have negative values, create and add a custom colormap for better visualization
if min_val < 0:
    # Create a proper diverging colormap
    colormap = cm.LinearColormap(
        colors=['#053061', '#2166AC', '#FFFFFF', '#B2182B', '#67001F'],  # Blue to White to Red
        index=[min_val, min_val/2, 0, max_val/2, max_val],
        vmin=min_val,
        vmax=max_val,
        caption='Percentage Stay (%) - Blue: Negative (Outflow), Red: Positive (Inflow)'
    )
    
    # Remove the default legend
    for key in choropleth._children:
        if key.startswith('color_map'):
            del(choropleth._children[key])
    
    # Add our custom colormap
    colormap.add_to(m)

# Add tooltips for each country including the 'Percentage stay' value
folium.GeoJson(
    geojson_data,
    style_function=lambda x: {'fillColor': 'transparent', 'color': 'black', 'weight': 0.5},
    tooltip=folium.GeoJsonTooltip(
        fields=['name', 'Percentage stay'],
        aliases=['Country:', 'Percentage Stay:']
    )
).add_to(m)

# Save the map to an HTML file
m.save('percentage_stay_map_2024.html')

# Display the map
m

# Trying to distinguish between 0 and 10 with colour
# Initialize a folium map
m = folium.Map(location=[20, 0], zoom_start=2)

# Add the properties to the GeoJSON as before
for feature in geojson_data['features']:
    country_name = feature['properties']['name']
    stay_value = merged_df.loc[merged_df['Citizenship'] == country_name, 'Percentage stay']
    feature['properties']['Percentage stay'] = (
        str(stay_value.values[0]) if not stay_value.empty else 'N/A'
    )

# Create a step-based custom colormap instead of using Choropleth
# First, let's create a StepColormap with our exact requirements

# Find Somalia's value (the negative one)
min_val = merged_df['Percentage stay'].min()
max_val = merged_df['Percentage stay'].max()

# Create a step colormap with exact breakpoints
step_colors = [
    '#2166AC',  # Blue for negative values (Somalia)
    '#FFFFFF',  # White for 0%
    '#FFFFCC',  # Very light yellow for 1-5%
    '#FFEDA0',  # Darker yellow for 5-10%
    '#FEB24C',  # Light orange for 10-25%
    '#FD8D3C',  # Orange for 25-50%
    '#E31A1C',  # Red for 50-75%
    '#800026'   # Dark red for 75-100%
]

# Define the exact breakpoints we want
if min_val < 0:
    step_thresholds = [min_val, 0, 1, 5, 10, 25, 50, 75, max_val]
else:
    step_thresholds = [0, 1, 5, 10, 25, 50, 75, max_val]
    step_colors = step_colors[1:]  # Remove the blue if no negative values

# Create a step colormap
step_colormap = cm.StepColormap(
    colors=step_colors,
    index=step_thresholds,
    vmin=min_val,
    vmax=max_val,
    caption='Percentage Stay (%)'
)

# Now create a GeoJson layer with style function using our step colormap
def style_function(feature):
    value = feature['properties'].get('Percentage stay', 'N/A')
    if value == 'N/A':
        return {'fillColor': '#F5F5F5', 'color': 'gray', 'weight': 0.5, 'fillOpacity': 0.7}
    
    try:
        value = float(value)
        color = step_colormap(value)
        return {'fillColor': color, 'color': 'black', 'weight': 0.5, 'fillOpacity': 0.7}
    except:
        return {'fillColor': '#F5F5F5', 'color': 'gray', 'weight': 0.5, 'fillOpacity': 0.7}

# Add the styled GeoJson layer
folium.GeoJson(
    geojson_data,
    style_function=style_function,
    tooltip=folium.GeoJsonTooltip(
        fields=['name', 'Percentage stay'],
        aliases=['Country:', 'Percentage Stay:']
    )
).add_to(m)

# Add the colormap to the map
step_colormap.add_to(m)

# Save the map to an HTML file
m.save('percentage_stay_map_2024.html')

# Display the map
m

df_2023 = pd.read_csv('net_migration_2023.csv', encoding='ISO-8859-1')
df_2024 = pd.read_csv('net_migration_2024.csv', encoding='ISO-8859-1')
In [11]:
# First, let's add a year column to each dataframe to track the source
df_2023['Year'] = 2023
df_2024['Year'] = 2024

# Rename the columns to include the year, except for Citizenship
df_2023_renamed = df_2023.rename(columns={
    'Immigration': 'Immigration_2023',
    'Emigration': 'Emigration_2023',
    'Net migration': 'Net_migration_2023',
    'Percentage stay': 'Percentage_stay_2023'
})

df_2024_renamed = df_2024.rename(columns={
    'Immigration': 'Immigration_2024',
    'Emigration': 'Emigration_2024',
    'Net migration': 'Net_migration_2024',
    'Percentage stay': 'Percentage_stay_2024'
})

# Perform an outer join on Citizenship
migration_comparison_df = pd.merge(
    df_2023_renamed, 
    df_2024_renamed,
    on='Citizenship',
    how='outer'
)

# Drop the duplicate Year columns that were created with suffixes
migration_comparison_df = migration_comparison_df.drop(columns=['Year_x', 'Year_y'])

# Calculate the change in percentage stay
migration_comparison_df['Percentage_stay_change'] = migration_comparison_df['Percentage_stay_2024'] - migration_comparison_df['Percentage_stay_2023']

# Sort by the absolute value of the change to see the biggest shifts
migration_comparison_df['Absolute_change'] = migration_comparison_df['Percentage_stay_change'].abs()
migration_trends_df = migration_comparison_df.sort_values('Absolute_change', ascending=False)

# Display the result with better formatting
pd.set_option('display.max_columns', None)  # Show all columns
pd.set_option('display.width', 1000)        # Wider display
pd.set_option('display.colheader_justify', 'center')

filtered_trends_df = migration_trends_df[(migration_trends_df['Net_migration_2024'] < -500) | 
                                        (migration_trends_df['Net_migration_2024'] > 500)]

# Keep both the direction of change and the magnitude
filtered_trends_df = filtered_trends_df[['Citizenship', 'Percentage_stay_change', 'Absolute_change']]

# Sort by Percentage_stay_change (descending order - highest positive change first)
filtered_trends_df = filtered_trends_df.sort_values(by='Percentage_stay_change', ascending=False)

# Reset the index
filtered_trends_df = filtered_trends_df.reset_index(drop=True)

# Apply custom styling
cvs.setup_styling()


# Filter for countries with absolute change of 5 percentage points or more
significant_changes = filtered_trends_df[
    (filtered_trends_df['Citizenship'] != 'Somalia') & 
    (filtered_trends_df['Absolute_change'] >= 5)
]

# Sort by the actual percentage change value
significant_changes = significant_changes.sort_values('Percentage_stay_change', ascending=False)

# Create a figure with appropriate size
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 10))

# Create horizontal bars
bars = ax.barh(significant_changes['Citizenship'], significant_changes['Percentage_stay_change'])

# Color the bars based on direction of change
for i, bar in enumerate(bars):
    if significant_changes['Percentage_stay_change'].iloc[i] < 0:
        bar.set_color(cvs.ORANGE)  # Use amber for decreases
    else:
        bar.set_color(cvs.TEAL)  # Use teal for increases

# Apply styling
cvs.apply_chart_style(
    ax,
    title="Change in Retention Percentage (2023-2024)",
    xlabel="Percentage Point Change",
    ylabel="Citizenship",
    grid=True
)

# Add a vertical line at x=0 to clearly separate increases and decreases
ax.axvline(x=0, color=cvs.COLORS['gray_dark'], linestyle='-', linewidth=1)



# Add a note about Somalia being excluded
note_text = f"Note: Somalia excluded with extreme change of -56.1%"
plt.figtext(0.5, 0.01, note_text, ha='center', fontsize=9, 
            style='italic', color=cvs.COLORS['gray_dark'])

# Adjust layout
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.03, 1, 1])

# Save the figure
cvs.savefig_with_background(fig, "retention_rate_change_2023_2024.png")

# Show the plot
plt.show()
